_meta.design: 8 behavioral-fit axes, each a reciprocal pair (2 poles). Poles chosen so neither is generically 'better' under default assistant norms; the deterministic pole-balance screen (|Δ global-desirability|<0.15) gates which pairs survive to mass generation. Seeds are expanded to full behavioral briefs (used for BOTH generation-conditioning and target-conditioned judging).
_meta.privacy: no real names; abstract behavioral handles only

pairs.axis_description: how candid vs cushioned the person wants critique and bad news

personas.essence: Wants the unvarnished read first; treats hedging and cushioning as condescension that wastes their time.
tells: impatient with caveats before the point
serves: name the flaw plainly then the fix
alienates: softening with 'one small thing to maybe consider'

personas.essence: Hears blunt critique as harshness and shuts down; needs the relational frame and what's working before what isn't.
serves: pair each flaw with what's salvageable

pairs.axis_description: whether the person wants a fan of options or a single recommended call

personas.essence: Wants the option space and tradeoffs laid out so they can decide; a single recommendation feels presumptuous and pre-empts their judgment.
tells: wants the reasoning to evaluate it themselves
serves: lay out 2-4 options with honest tradeoffs
alienates: a single answer with no fan-out

personas.essence: Wants a clear recommended action with the why; an option menu reads as the assistant dodging the hard part and leaves them stuck.
tells: wants a default to react to
serves: give one recommended call up front
offer the runner-up only if close

pairs.axis_description: whether feelings get acknowledged before problem-solving

personas.essence: Needs the emotional reality named before any fixing; jumping straight to solutions reads as cold and unseen.
serves: acknowledge the feeling first and specifically
alienates: treating distress as a ticket to close

personas.essence: Wants the problem addressed; emotional acknowledgment feels like stalling or being managed, and lands as condescending.
tells: 'I don't need a pep talk, I need a fix'
serves: go straight to the concrete fix

personas.essence: Wants momentum and a bias to action; exhaustive risk-listing reads as hand-wringing that kills the move.
serves: back the move, then the one real risk
alienates: leading with everything that could go wrong

personas.essence: Wants failure modes named and reversibility checked before committing; bias-to-action feels reckless and unsafe.
serves: endorse only after the downside is mapped

pairs.axis_description: whether the person wants their reasoning stress-tested or steadied

personas.essence: Wants their thinking attacked at its weak points; agreement and reassurance feel useless and a little insulting.
Is often deciding while shaky; well-meant pushback when fragile lands as piling on and erodes the confidence to act.
Wants the full reasoning, caveats and edge cases; terse bottom-line answers feel dismissive and untrustworthy.
serves: name the caveats and edge cases

personas.essence: Wants the answer in the first sentence and will ask for more if needed; long reasoning reads as noise burying the point.
alienates: making them dig for the answer

personas.pole: wants to be treated as the expert
personas.essence: Is highly capable in-domain and wants peer-level engagement; step-by-step hand-holding reads as condescending.
Is out of their depth and wants explicit structure and steps; assuming expertise leaves them lost and ashamed to ask.
Wants a concrete plan, checklist or structure to act on; open-ended exploration feels unmoored and anxiety-making.
serves: close the loop with next actions

personas.essence: Thinks by exploring possibilities out loud; premature structure feels constraining and forecloses the good idea.
serves: defer structure until the shape emerges
